spec_features.spec_quote: the episode is cut short — we've already observed what we're measuring; further turns just burn tokens
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:60 sets early_pred = in_progress_degraded if config.early_stop_after_degraded_turns; passed to run_episode as degraded_so_far. agent.py:214-220: if config.early_stop_after_degraded_turns and degraded_so_far -> increments degraded_streak, and 'if degraded_streak >= config.early_stop_after_degraded_turns: transcript.terminal_reason = TERMINAL_EARLY_STOP; break'. The predicate runs each turn, the streak is counted, compared, and the loop actually breaks. default early_stop_after_degraded_turns=6 (config.py).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: predicate computed, streak compared, loop broken with TERMINAL_EARLY_STOP. Disable-able via config=0.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py: 'for turn_index in range(1, config.max_turns + 1):' with a for/else 'else: transcript.terminal_reason = TERMINAL_MAX_TURNS'. config.py: max_turns: int = 30. The cap bounds the loop and sets the terminal reason when exhausted.

spec_features.spec_quote: Once the cheap per-turn predicate flags degradation for several consecutive turns, the episode is cut short
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py in_progress_degraded() is a per-turn check of the most recent turn (self-criticism+repetition, repeated identical action, or degenerate text). agent.py:214-220 calls it each turn, increments degraded_streak on True / resets on False, and breaks when streak >= threshold. This is the same enforced mechanism as the early-stop above; monitoring drives the cut-short.
spec_features.notes: Per-turn predicate genuinely computed and acted on; conservative (requires consecutive streak).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early stop once degradation is unmistakable, to save tokens.

spec_features.spec_quote: noticing the rigging and stopping cleanly is exactly the graceful behavior the judge rewards
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:174-179: 'if not calls:' (model ended its turn with no tool call) -> 'transcript.terminal_reason = TERMINAL_GAVE_UP; break'. The model's choice to stop is honored as a terminal state and the loop exits. schemas.py:93 TERMINAL_GAVE_UP. There is no dedicated exit/finish tool — the exit path is simply ending a turn without a tool call, which the loop honors.
spec_features.notes: The subject is not offered an explicit exit tool; it can only exit by emitting no tool call. That is honored. The 'judge rewards graceful' part (graceful_handling dimension) only scores; it does not change subject treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool call => the model ended its turn. In an unsolvable task this is either a graceful stop or a giving-up.
